method: Instruction listings decoded directly from the PE bytes of the identified executable through its section table, with the executable size and SHA-256 verified first. Every cited locator address was checked to begin an instruction of its decoded function, and the operands, name literals, vftable cells, jump table entries, constants and call targets named in the claims were compared with those listings by a second pass. Callers were enumerated by scanning the .text section for rel32 call and jmp instructions, so virtual and indirect callers are not covered. Addresses are absolute virtual addresses. The MEASURED facts are call-site and script counts that agree with xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json. Script argument counts, constants and descriptor selectors come from a local Lua 5.1 bytecode scan that no tracked artifact carries and are INFERRED. No decompiled body is a tracked evidence dependency.
scope: Static Lua call contracts of fifteen native registrations of the DesktopWidget, CharaBase, NpcBase, WorldMaster, PlayerBase and CutScene classes: _setTargetNearestCharacter, _updateItemPackage, _getExtendedTemporaryGroup, _setReactionTriggerBox, _transformIntoChocobo (two registrations), _isDoneAchievement, _getSubStatStatus, _getLastAttacker, _loadCutScene, _getSystemFlag, _getAchievementSheetDataTitle, _getAchievementSheetDataItem, _getAchievementRate and _getAchievementItemId. Each row gives the registration site, receiver type check, declared argument and return lists, branches, reads, client state effects, failure behavior and yield behavior. Client-side contracts do not establish target selection rules, group membership, item package contents, achievement values, reaction record contents or server behavior.
evidenceTier: MIXED, see tierVocabulary and the tier of each fact

framework.reference: manifests/chara_world_native_call_contract.json framework and manifests/item_native_call_contract.json framework: registration, the 0x00CC9D60 type registry, argument marshalling through 0x00D19A20, the holder receiver adapter, the cell tags, the invalid-parameter route, the return pushers, the world object chain and the yield request. Each registrar builds the return list first and the argument list second.

registration.note: The order of a native is its position among the rel32 calls of its switchboard, counted from 1. Each registrar has one rel32 caller in .text, recorded as registrarCaller. Each switchboard call sits behind a test of the byte at +0x0E of the switchboard argument. A nonzero byte adds 1 to the word at +0x0C and skips the registrar.

widget/desktopwidget_u defines a plain Lua function _setTargetNearestCharacter on DesktopWidget. It returns false when work.targetCursorMask is true, returns false when the current target cursor is 1 and the local player has a lock-on target, and otherwise calls self:_setTargetNearestCharacter_cpp(n) and returns true. The seven script call sites call the plain function, not the registered native. This comes from a local bytecode scan that no tracked artifact carries.
The callback tests the cell vector size, reads cell 0 as an int through 0x005819A0 and stores the low byte at receiver +0x78.

It takes R from 0x00CC7510 on the dword at ExecuteParameters +0x04, X = [R] and Y = [X +0x04], loads the dword at Y +0x04 and calls 0x0075B720 with it. The callback then stores the byte 0 at receiver +0x78. It does not read the answer of the call.

0x0075B720 loads the first dword of its argument, takes the object at its +0x4C0 through 0x004D7310 and tail jumps to 0x005656B0 with it. The routine 0x005656B0 answers false when the signed dword at +0xB8 of that object is negative. Otherwise it calls 0x005655F0 with the argument 1. A nonzero result and the dword at +0xB8 go to 0x00562D30 and it answers true.
0x00562D30 contains a path that, when 0x004D7430 on the dword at +0x7C of its object answers nonzero, builds a record with the dwords 0xCD and 0x18 and passes it to 0x004D6D10.

The serverbound opcode 0x00CD is SetTargetPacket in xivl-opcodes:opcodes.json, so a successful selection can reach the SetTarget request. The selection conditions inside 0x005655F0 and 0x00562D30 were not traced.
The reader of the byte at receiver +0x78 and the effect of the byte on the selection were not found in the traced routines.

rows.callbackKind: thin adapter into a body routine

arguments.note: Group selector. The script sites pass 10001 and 10002 or a variable.

returns.note: GroupBase control, or nil when the group is not valid.

rows.behavior: The sibling of _getGroup. It calls the same helper with the flag 1. The helper reads one int, asks the group manager of the world object for the group of the receiver identity and that int, and pushes a GroupBase control for a valid group or nil. The flag selects creation mode 1 of the control factory instead of mode 0. It requests no yield.

branches.condition: The group manager at Y +0xE4 answers a valid group for the receiver identity and the int
pushes: LuaControl*: a GroupBase control created in mode 1

branches.condition: The group is not valid

facts.claim: The callback pushes the flag 1 and the ExecuteParameters pointer and calls the helper 0x00701140. The _getGroup callback 0x007083F0 calls the same helper with the flag 0.

The helper tests the cell vector size, reads cell 0 as an int through 0x005819A0, takes the dword at +0xE4 of Y and calls 0x006C4560 on it with the address of the ExecuteParameters identity at +0x0C and the address of the int. 0x006CB950 tests the result and a failed test pushes nil through 0x00748920.
A valid result goes to 0x006E2240 with the flag and the group handle. The returned control is pushed through 0x00748B30.

0x006E2240 tests its flag byte at 0x006E22EF. A zero flag calls 0x00CC80A0 and a nonzero flag calls 0x00CC8140. Both are thin wrappers of the control factory 0x00CD9360 and differ only in the mode dword that they store before the call, 0 at 0x00CC80C8 and 1 at 0x00CC8168. The control is then cast to GroupBase and 16 bytes of the group handle are copied to control +0x68.

What the creation mode does inside 0x00CD9360, and so what a script sees that differs between a control from _getGroup and one from _getExtendedTemporaryGroup, was not traced. The group manager contents and the meaning of the int selector were not traced either.

facts.claim: The callback tests the cell vector size, reads cell 0 as an int and, after a second size test that needs more than 1 cell, reads cell 1 as an int. Both reads use 0x005819A0.
It takes R from 0x00CC7510 on the dword at ExecuteParameters +0x04, X = [R] and Y = [X +0x04] and builds the control list through 0x00CC88D0.

For each control it casts from LuaControl 0x01270B4C to the type descriptor 0x012C1964, which the holder table gives to WidgetBase. For a nonnull cast it obtains a string through 0x00CC7560 and compares it with the literal at 0x00FD4E38, TargetParameterWidget, through 0x00445D60, a C string compare that answers whether the two are equal. That the string is the control name is INFERRED.

For a matching control it builds the strings Hidden (0x00FD4E50), Visibility (0x00FD4E58) and Window_TargetParameterWidget (0x00FD4E64) and calls 0x0075B810 on the dword at Y +0x04. The role of that call is INFERRED from the strings to hide the target parameter window.

It then builds an actor class visitor with the vftable 0x00FD590C, whose RTTI name is s_CharaIterateActorClass with the base CharaIterateInterface. The visitor keeps the first int at +0x08 and a result slot at +0x0C. 0x00764150 walks the container at V +0x4E4, which 0x004D73A0 returns, and calls visitor slot 1 with the key at node +0x0C of each node. It stops when a visit answers 0.

The visit method 0x007179A0 resolves the visited identity to a control through 0x00CC7A50, casts it to NpcBase with the type descriptor 0x012709E4 and requires the byte at control +0x5C to be nonzero. It reads the work value of the key 0x1389 through 0x00CC7B90 and, when that equals the visitor dword at +0x08, stores the identity at visitor +0x0C and answers 0.

The callback then calls 0x0075F3A0 with the address of a local that receives the chara pointer, the address of the visitor result slot and the second int. 0x0075F3A0 reads the identity from the slot, finds the chara through 0x004D9970, calls 0x00589D30 with the second int and calls 0x004D7980 with the type 0x17.
0x00589D30 sign extends the low byte of its argument, clears bit 2 of the chara byte at +0x26D and calls 0x004D7980 with the type 9 and a 4 byte payload that holds the sign extended byte.

The callback allocates 8 bytes through 0x009D1B35 and builds a resume checker with the vftable 0x00FD5918, whose RTTI name is s_WaitForTransformIntoChocoboResumeChecker with the base ResumeCheckerInterface. The checker keeps the chara pointer at +0x04. The yield request 0x00CD2860 receives it with the Lua thread at ExecuteParameters +0x08.

The visitor result slot at visitor +0x0C starts at 0 (ebx is zeroed at 0x006EC62B and stored at 0x006EC8F3) and only a matching visit writes it. When no NpcBase actor has the work key 0x1389 equal to the first int, 0x0075F3A0 still passes the identity 0 to 0x004D9970. That routine adds 0x4AC to the receiver and jumps to 0x004DE190, which answers 0 for the identity 0xC0000000 at 0x004DE19D and for an identity that is not in its map at 0x004DE1F9.

0x0075F3A0 does not test the chara pointer that it receives. 0x0075F3B8 calls 0x00589D30 with that pointer in ECX, and 0x00589D30 executes an AND on the byte at chara +0x26D at 0x00589D35 before any other use of ECX. A null chara therefore dereferences the address 0x0000026D in retail. The call 0x004D7980 with the type 0x17 and the yield request 0x00CD2860 come after that point. The run-time effect was not run.
The poll of the resume checker, the meaning of the work key 0x1389 and of the type 0x17 and type 9 payloads, and the effect of the hidden widget on a script were not traced.

Whether the identity 0 can be a key of the map that 0x004DE190 searches was not traced. A missing key answers a null chara, and a present key 0 would answer a chara that was not selected by the work key.

rows.callbackKind: thin thunk into a virtual slot

returns.note: True when the bit that the id maps to is set in the overall achievement bitset.

rows.behavior: Dispatches through the PlayerBase vftable slot 101. The MyPlayer routine maps the id to a bit index through 0x0070AB40 and pushes whether that bit is set in the bitset at the start of the achievement store that the dword at MyPlayer +0x114 addresses. Other players push nothing. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback 0x0071E550 is a thunk of three instructions. It loads the vftable of the receiver, loads the dword at vftable +0x194 (slot 101) and jumps to it.

The PlayerBase vftable 0x00FD5E04 holds 0x00776340 in the cell 0x00FD5F98. That routine is the single instruction ret 4, so a receiver whose class does not override the slot pushes nothing. The MyPlayer vftable 0x00FD785C holds 0x00705A70 in the cell 0x00FD79F0.
The MyPlayer routine tests the cell vector size, reads cell 0 as an int through 0x005819A0 and loads the achievement store pointer from MyPlayer +0x114. It calls 0x0070AB40 with the id.

0x0070AB40 subtracts 100 from the id and, for a result above 0x7BE, answers 0. Otherwise it jumps through the 0x7BF cell table at 0x0070BCB4. Each cell loads a constant and returns it. 740 cells return distinct bit indexes from 1 to 1023 and the other 1243 cells return 0. Only the ids 100 to 2082 can have a nonzero bit index. An id outside the table range jumps to 0x0070BCB1, which returns 0, and every zero cell returns 0, so such an id tests bit 0 of the bitset.

A bit index of 0x400 or more calls 0x006B4AF0, which builds the message invalid bitset<N> position from the literal at 0x00FA6EF4 and throws it. No table cell returns such an index. The test then checks the bit (index and 0x1F) of the dword at store + 4 times (index shifted right by 5), and the answer is pushed through 0x00748870.

The MyPlayer override 0x006F3420 allocates the achievement store with 0xAC bytes at 0x006F3598. The player misc native contract (docs/player-misc-native-contract.md, section Grand Company rank) records its constructor and the zeroed range before the vector at +0x80.
The achievement store is a bitset of 1024 bits followed by a dword vector at store +0x80. The sizes come from the bitset message, the test above and the vector reads of _getAchievementItemId.
The writers of the bitset, the meaning of each bit and the values that a server sends were not traced here.
